title: Add a matrix of built R / Python / Quarto versions to README
description: Help me browse available images quickly by providing a table or matrix of the built R / Python / Quarto versions in the readme. Browsing available tags in DockerHub is slow and harder to parse out if I'm looking for a particular set of versions.

title: Add quarto version to tag
description: When adding an execution environment to Connect, you must specify the R, Python, and Quarto installation versions and executable paths.  The R and Python versions are distinguishable by the tag name, but the Quarto version is undetermined. I cannot add this executable to my Connect execution environments without knowing the version.

title: Consider adding optional system packages for Connect Standard image
description: If a user runs the Connect Standard in local execution mode (standalone), there are many basic system packages missing that are required for executing content such as Shiny apps. We should consider adding these libraries to the standard image for better out-of-the-box support of various types of content.

title: Create a `connect-runtime` image for use with Kubernetes ImageVolumes
description:
Add a new `connect-runtime` image. The tagging scheme should be `connect-runtime:{$connect_version}`

The runtime is built with the lowest supported glibc so this image should be compatible with all distributions. It is suitable for mounting directly to the `Kubernetes.ConnectRuntimeDir` as an ImageVolume w/o needing to perform an init-container copy operation.

The dockerfile is simply:

```Dockerfile
FROM scratch
ARG TARGETARCH=rockylinux
ADD packaging/build/rstudio-connect-runtime*-${TARGETARCH}.tar.gz /
```

title: Content images with NVIDIA support
description:
Original issue: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/issues/521

Ey up!

Due to another issue (see https://github.com/rstudio/helm/issues/355), I've not been able to find out whether CUDA apps would work using the content images from Posit. In the event that they don't, I've prepared a Dockerfile based on [NVIDIA's Dockerfile](https://gitlab.com/nvidia/container-images/cuda/-/blob/master/dist/11.4.3/ubuntu1804/base/Dockerfile).

The only change I made was to replace:

`FROM ubuntu:18.04 as base`

with:

`FROM rstudio/content-base:r4.1.0-py3.9.2-ubuntu1804 as base`

in the hope that it would become an image that works on Posit Connect and can use GPU with the CUDA apps. See below for the full Dockerfile.

I'd be interested to know if this is how Posit team would do it, whether actually the base Posit content images already had CUDA support, or if you would do it differently.

Thank you!

Ben

```
FROM rstudio/content-base:r4.1.0-py3.9.2-ubuntu1804 as base

FROM base as base-amd64

ENV NVARCH x86_64

ENV NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA "cuda>=11.4 brand=tesla,driver>=418,driver<419 brand=tesla,driver>=450,driver<451"
ENV NV_CUDA_CUDART_VERSION 11.4.148-1
ENV NV_CUDA_COMPAT_PACKAGE cuda-compat-11-4

FROM base as base-arm64

ENV NVARCH sbsa
ENV NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA "cuda>=11.4"
ENV NV_CUDA_CUDART_VERSION 11.4.148-1

FROM base-${TARGETARCH}

ARG TARGETARCH

LABEL maintainer "NVIDIA CORPORATION <cudatools@nvidia.com>"

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    gnupg2 curl ca-certificates && \
    curl -fsSL https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu1804/${NVARCH}/3bf863cc.pub | apt-key add - && \
    echo "deb https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu1804/${NVARCH} /" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cuda.list && \
    apt-get purge --autoremove -y curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV CUDA_VERSION 11.4.3

# For libraries in the cuda-compat-* package: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/eula/index.html#attachment-a
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    cuda-cudart-11-4=${NV_CUDA_CUDART_VERSION} \
    ${NV_CUDA_COMPAT_PACKAGE} \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Required for nvidia-docker v1
RUN echo "/usr/local/nvidia/lib" >> /etc/ld.so.conf.d/nvidia.conf \
    && echo "/usr/local/nvidia/lib64" >> /etc/ld.so.conf.d/nvidia.conf

ENV PATH /usr/local/nvidia/bin:/usr/local/cuda/bin:${PATH}
ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH /usr/local/nvidia/lib:/usr/local/nvidia/lib64

COPY NGC-DL-CONTAINER-LICENSE /

# nvidia-container-runtime
ENV NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES all
ENV NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES compute,utility
```

title: Evaluate adding R/Py to $PATH in Connect Content images
description:
Original Issue https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/issues/821

In our connect content images currently neither R nor Py are referenced in $PATH. In certain cases this can create unexpected errors -- I discovered this via using Databricks with Connect, where the R Databricks packages require reticulate, python and rpy2, and do not build without R referenced in $PATH. I confirmed via custom image where I added `ENV PATH=$PATH:/opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin` that adding R and Py to $PATH fixes the above issue.

title: Set `HTTP.NoWarning` to `true` in `rstudio-connect.gcfg`?
description:
Original Issue: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/issues/888

When running a Connect container with the default configuration there is a warning at the top about using plain insecure HTTP instead of the secure HTTPS. In the context of running the container locally and accessing at http://localhost:3939 this warning is unnecessary. Since someone running this container with HTTPS will either need to modify `rstudio-connect.gcfg` or run behind a proxy, would it make sense to set [`HTTP.NoWarning`](https://docs.posit.co/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/#HTTP.NoWarning) to `true` for the built-in `rstudio-connect.gcfg` file?

Files:
- <https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/blob/dev/connect/rstudio-connect.gcfg>
- <https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio-docker-products/blob/dev/connect/rstudio-connect-float.gcfg>

title: Add RHEL 10 (UBI) support for connect-content / connect-content-init
description:
Phase 3 of the RHEL 10 (UBI) initiative (posit-dev/images-shared#575).

Extends RHEL 10 (UBI) support to the `connect-content` (R x Python
matrix) and `connect-content-init` images, once base `connect` support
(posit-dev/images-connect#143) lands.

## Notes

Blocked by #143 — the matrix images build on that pattern.

title: Add RHEL 10 (UBI) support for connect (Standard/Minimal)
description:
Phase 2 of the RHEL 10 (UBI) initiative (posit-dev/images-shared#575).

Connect has no RHEL/UBI support today — this is first-time enablement,
not a port of an existing pattern. posit-dev/images-package-manager#130
(RHEL 10 UBI support) is the closest precedent: Containerfile.rhel10.std/min,
deps/rhel-10_packages.txt, and an install script wired through the shared
`dnf.j2` macro.

## Approach

- Standard and Minimal builds on `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi`,
  amd64 + arm64
- Validate R, Python, and Quarto install and run correctly on RHEL 10
  (requires R 4.6.1+ to avoid the flexiblas-devel issue fixed in
  rstudio/r-builds#329)
- Fix the RHEL 10 gap in `posit_product/main.py`'s distro-tag resolver
  (`ProductEnum.CONNECT` branch handles versions 8/9 but falls through to
  `"multi"` for 10)

## Notes

Out of scope: `connect-content`/`connect-content-init` (tracked
separately).

title: Pin Ubuntu 26.04 images to GNU coreutils as a workaround for a Connect runtime incompatibility
description:
## Summary

Ubuntu 26.04 switched its default core utilities from GNU coreutils to the new
Rust-based implementation (`rust-coreutils` / uutils). These are documented by
Ubuntu as "not fully compatible yet" with GNU coreutils, and this incompatibility
appears to cause a defect in the Posit Connect runtime on Ubuntu 26.04.

Rather than pausing Ubuntu 26.04 builds, we will pin the Ubuntu 26.04 images back
to GNU coreutils as a workaround so the images continue to build and run correctly.
We will move to the Rust-based utilities in a future release once the runtime is
confirmed compatible upstream.

## Background

- Ubuntu 26.04 provides core utilities via the Rust-based `rust-coreutils` package
  by default. Ubuntu's own release notes note these are not fully GNU-compatible yet.
- Ubuntu supports switching the provider back to GNU coreutils with a dedicated
  package: `coreutils-from-gnu`.
- Behavioral differences in the core utilities are the suspected cause of the
  Connect runtime defect observed on Ubuntu 26.04.

## Proposed change

Update the Ubuntu 26.04 image definitions to install GNU coreutils early in the
build so both the build and the resulting runtime use GNU utilities:

    apt-get install -y coreutils-from-gnu --allow-remove-essential

Apply this to the affected Ubuntu 26.04 variants of the `connect` and
`connect-content` images (including development/preview builds). Ubuntu 22.04 and
24.04 images are unaffected. `connect-content-init` is unaffected (it has no
Ubuntu 26.04 variant).

## Validation

- [ ] Build the Ubuntu 26.04 images with the GNU coreutils swap applied.
- [ ] Confirm the reported runtime defect no longer reproduces.
- [ ] Confirm existing test suites pass on the updated Ubuntu 26.04 images.

## Follow-up

- This is a temporary workaround. Once the Connect runtime is confirmed compatible
  with the Rust-based core utilities upstream, revert the pin (switch back to
  `coreutils-from-uutils` / the Ubuntu default) in a subsequent release.
